title: Protocol for clickable photoaffinity labeling and quantitative chemical proteomics
protocol: Culture one 15 cm plate of light CCF cells and one 15 cm plate of heavy CCF cells to 90% confluence in appropriate SILAC media.
Wash each plate twice with ice cold Dulbecco’s phosphate buffered saline (DPBS, 2 × 30 mL) to remove FBS from the culture medium.
Dissolve compound 1 in culture media without FBS.
Pre-treat light cells with compound 1 for 30 min (25 μM, 0.5% DMSO, 37°C and 5% CO2) in cell media without FBS.
Pre-treat heavy cells with DMSO for 30 min in cell media without FBS.
Add compound 2 (0.1% DMSO, 500 nM) to both light and heavy cells for 30 min (37°C, 5% CO2).
Wash both cells with ice cold serum free media (2 × 25 mL).
Perform UV irradiation for both plates using a custom modified Rayonet apparatus (360 nm, 4°C).
Wash both plates with ice cold DPBS buffer (2 × 30 mL).
Aspirate media during each wash.
Scrape cells in ice cold DPBS buffer (15 mL) using a cell scraper.
Place both light and heavy cells into UV apparatus together.
Shake system gently at 50 rpm and 4°C.
Remove culture plate lids to enhance irradiation efficiency.
Centrifuge cells at 1000 × g for 10 min to pellet them.
Pipette or aspirate DPBS buffer from the cells, leaving minimal volume.
Store cell pellets at −80°C.
Repeat steps 3 to 8 for reverse SILAC, treating light cells with DMSO instead of 1.
For probe vs. probe controls, repeat steps 3 to 8 without pre-treatment of either condition before adding 2.
For probe vs. no probe controls, do not pre-treat light and heavy cells; add 2 to heavy cells and DMSO to light cells for a 30 min incubation.
For UV vs. no-UV controls, repeat steps 3 to 8 with 1 added to both conditions but perform UV irradiation only on heavy cells while keeping light cells in the dark at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Re-suspend heavy cell pellet with 0.5 mL DPBS buffer pH 7.2.
Re-suspend light cell pellet with 0.5 mL DPBS buffer pH 7.2.
Dilute benzonase (25 kU/mL) by adding 6 μL of stock to 60 μL DPBS buffer pH 7.2.
Add 5 μL diluted benzonase to each sample.
Incubate samples at 10 min at 20°C–25°C while shaking.
Centrifuge samples at 5000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Take the supernatant for subsequent steps.
Lyse cells at 4°C with probe sonication using a Fisherbrand Model 120 Sonic Dismembrator with settings: 1 s on, 1 s off pulses for 20 s at 75% amplitude.
Determine protein concentrations with BCA assay.
Pipette 5 μL of sample into each well of a 96-well plate.
Add 20 μL of DPBS buffer pH 7.2 to each well for a 1:5 dilution.
For triplicate measurements, add 16 μL sample to 64 μL DPBS buffer and then pipette 25 μL into three separate wells.
Prepare BSA protein standards using various concentrations (3, 2.4, 1.9, 1.5, 1.2, 1, 0.8, 0.63, 0.5 mg/mL) diluted in PBS buffer.
Add 200 μL of working reagent to each well and shake for 30 minutes at 37°C in the dark.
Read absorbance at 562 nm using a Tecan Infinite 200 PRO plate reader.
Adjust lysate volumes with lysis buffer to achieve a final concentration of 2 mg/mL in a volume of 0.5 mL.
Mix equal protein amounts of heavy and light cell lysates together to reach a final total volume of 1 mL.
Ultracentrifuge samples at 100,000 × g for 50 minutes to separate soluble and membrane fractions (optional).
Solubilize the membrane fraction with 0.5 mL of lysis buffer before proceeding (if ultracentrifugation is performed).
Perform CuAAC chemistry reaction by treating samples with 41 μL click chemistry master mix.
Incubate samples at 20°C–25°C in the dark for 1 hour with end-to-end rotation using a rotisserie shaker.
Add 7.5 μL of LDS loading buffer (4×).
Add 3 μL of reducing agent DTT (10×).
Vortex and keep at 20°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Vortex again and centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 2 minutes.
Load 25 μL of sample to SDS-PAGE gel.
Run the gel at 120 V for 1 hour with MES running buffer until 20 kDa band reaches the end of the gel.
After electrophoresis, wash gels with deionized water 3 times.
Scan gels with a Typhoon FLA 9500 Biomolecular Imager using 532 nm laser excitation and 580 nm emission.
Fix gels in 50% MeOH/7% Acetic acid for 15 minutes.
Rinse fixed gels with 40% MeOH for at least 20 minutes before scanning.
Incubate gel with InstantBlue Coomassie blue reagent for 14 to 18 hours.
De-stain gel in water for 1 hour prior to scanning with Li-COR Odyssey CLx imaging system using the 700 nm channel.
Perform protein precipitation with leftover sample (∼0.5 mL) by chilling and adding ice-cold MeOH (0.5 mL) and cold CHCl3 (0.2 mL).
If the total volume of sample is ≥1 mL, transfer samples to a 15 mL falcon tube or a 5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Scale all MeOH and CHCl3 volumes to achieve a 4:4:1 aqueous: MeOH:CHCl3 ratio for efficient precipitation.
Vortex and add 0.5 mL of cold DPBS buffer.
Vortex again.
Centrifuge to separate the phases (5000 × g, 10 min).
Carefully remove liquid without disturbing protein disc before adding 1:1 MeOH: CHCl3 (0.5 mL).
Centrifuge at 5000 × g, 10 min.
Repeat wash in step twice more.
Re-suspend proteins by sonication in MeOH (2 mL).
Add CHCl3 (0.2 mL), vortex and pellet proteins by centrifugation (5000 × g, 10 min).
Air dry proteins for approximately 2 minutes before re-suspension with 150 μL of 10% SDS solution.
Mix well to re-suspend.
Add 0.5 mL of 8 M urea in 50 mM Tris, pH 8.0 buffer.
Perform sonication if necessary for protein re-suspension.
Reduce and alkylate proteins prior to enrichment.
Add dithiothreitol (DTT) to a final concentration of 10 mM (stock made in water).
Incubate samples for 30 min at 37°C while shaking.
Add iodoacetamide to samples to a final concentration of 12.5 mM.
Incubate samples for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C in the dark while shaking.
Dilute samples by adding 11 mL of 50 mM Tris pH 8.0 buffer.
Pipette high capacity streptavidin agarose resin (120 μL of 50% slurry per each sample) to a 15 mL falcon tube.
Pre-wash the resin with 50 mM Tris, pH 8.0 buffer (3 × 10 mL).
Add 100 μL of pre-washed streptavidin agarose resin (1:1 slurry in 50 mM Tris pH 8.0) to each sample.
Incubate samples for 14–18 hours at 4°C with end-to-end rotation.
Centrifuge samples at 1,500 × g for 3 minutes to isolate beads.
Discard the remaining buffer.
Add 0.1% SDS in DPBS (10 mL) and incubate with beads for 10 minutes with end-over-end rotation.
Centrifuge beads at 1,500 × g for 3 minutes and discard wash buffer.
Repeat the previous washing step two more times.
Add 50 mM Tris pH 8.0 (10 mL) and incubate with beads for 10 minutes with end-to-end rotation.
Centrifuge beads at 1,500 × g for 3 minutes and discard the wash buffer.
Repeat the previous two steps an additional two times.
For samples quantitated by TMT, use 50 mM HEPES pH 8.5 buffer instead of Tris buffers for washes.
Add distilled water (10 mL) and incubate with beads for 10 minutes with end-to-end rotation.
Centrifuge beads at 1,500 × g for 3 minutes and remove the water.
Washes in steps 24c and 24d are critical for removing SDS to avoid complications from detergent in MS-based analysis.
Perform on-bead digestion by adding trypsin mix to each sample.
Incubate samples for 14–18 hours shaking at 37°C.
For TMT-quantitated samples, use HEPES buffer instead of Tris during this step.
Isolate digested peptides from beads by placing the entire solution on Micro Bio-Spin columns (Bio-Rad).
Centrifuge (500 × g for 3 minutes) to collect eluant of digested peptides.
Collect washes with MS-grade water (100 μL) and pool them with the eluant.
Pooled eluant should be dried to near completion using a speed vacuum system.
Store peptides at -80°C.
Dissolve peptide samples in 1% TFA (40 μL) and desalt using C18 ZipTips (Millipore, 10 μL).
Activate the resin of C18 ZipTip with 1:1 acetonitrile:water (3 × 10 μL).
Wash the resin with 1% TFA in water (3 × 10 μL).
Load resin by pipetting in and out 30×, vortexing sample solution every 10×.
Wash resin with 1% TFA in water (3 × 10 μL).
Elute by pipetting 30× in 70% acetonitrile, 0.1% TFA.
Reconstitute peptides in 7 μL of 5% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid.
Run peptide samples by injecting 5 μL of sample through a trapping column (Acclaim PepMap C18 nanoViper LC column, 75 μm ID × 20 mm, 3 μm, 100 Å).
Transfer captured peptides through a C18 column (EASY-Spray LC column, C18, 75 μm ID × 50 cm, 2 μm, 100 Å) using an EASY-nanoLC 1200 equipped with an autosampler.
Use two buffers: 0.1% formic acid in water (A) and 0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile (B).
Elute peptides using a linear gradient of 1% to 35% B at a flow rate of 300 nL/min over 120 minutes.
Set standard mass spectrometry parameters for the SILAC-based approach.
For TMTpro, increase the linear gradient from 5 to 30% B at a flow rate of 250 nL/min over 98 minutes.
Follow with an increase in B from 30% to 45% in 20 minutes and then to 55% B over 10 minutes.
